title: Linear-time Rule Mining Under Formal Guarantees
abstract: arXiv:2409.16238v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Probabilistic logical models are a core component of neurosymbolic AI and are important in their own right for tasks that require high explainability. Unlike neural networks, logical theories that underlie the model are often handcrafted using domain expertise, making their development costly and prone to errors. While there are algorithms that learn logical theories from data, they are generally prohibitively expensive, limiting their applicability in real-world settings. Here, we introduce precision and recall for logical rules and define their composition as rule utility -- a measure of the predictive power of logical theories that can be computed in linear time in the data size. We then present SPECTRUM, a linear-time framework for learning logical theories from relational data, that mines recurrent patterns in the data, and subsequently uses our utility measure to evaluate and rank the rules derived from these patterns. translated_title: 形式化保证下的线性时间规则挖掘
translated_abstract: 概率逻辑模型是神经符号人工智能的核心组成部分，并且在需要高可解释性的任务中本身就具有重要价值。与神经网络不同，模型底层的逻辑理论通常需要依靠领域专业知识手工构建，这使得其开发成本高昂且容易出错。虽然已有从数据中学习逻辑理论的算法，但它们通常代价极其高昂，限制了其在现实场景中的应用。在本文中，我们为逻辑规则引入了精确率与召回率，并将二者的组合定义为规则效用——一种衡量逻辑理论预测能力的度量指标，其计算时间与数据规模呈线性关系。随后，我们提出了SPECTRUM，一个从关系数据中学习逻辑理论的线性时间框架，该框架挖掘数据中反复出现的模式，进而利用我们的效用度量对这些模式导出的规则进行评估和排序。
tldr: 该论文提出了可在线性时间内计算的规则效用度量，并据此构建了从关系数据中高效挖掘与评估逻辑规则的SPECTRUM框架，实现了形式化保证下的逻辑理论自动学习。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a linear-time computable rule utility measure and presents SPECTRUM, a framework that efficiently mines and ranks logical rules from relational data, enabling learning of logical theories under formal guarantees.
